architecture.name: hybrid-linear-attention-coverage
architecture.head_dims: The linear-attention side of the Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 hybrid family uses Gated DeltaNet heads with linear_key_head_dim 128 and linear_value_head_dim 128 (KDA element-wise-gating variant in some checkpoints); the kernel ecosystem that serves them is head-shape-generic: flash-linear-attention (FLA) Triton kernels autotune over head dims (v-head dims up to 256 supported, Qwen uses 128) with chunk size 64 (FLA_CHUNK_SIZE = 64, verified in vLLM's vendored copy vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/utils.py in the sm75-marlin tree), llama.cpp's CUDA kernel template-instantiates S_v in {16, 32, 64, 128} (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/gated_delta_net.cu), and TFLA (arXiv 2503.14376) demonstrates head dims to 256 and beyond. Contrast with the full-attention layers of the same models: head_dim 256 (see qwen35-architecture-deep-dive item).
architecture.qkv_dim_divergence: Within GDN layers, per-head k_dim == v_dim == 128, but K/V projection widths diverge via head COUNT: linear_num_key_heads 16 (K width 2048) vs linear_num_value_heads 48 (V width 6144) on the 27B dense models (16 K heads vs 32 V heads on Qwen3-Next-80B), so the recurrent state is a non-square 6144x2048 projection with per-(V-head) 128x128 state matrices - 3 V-heads share each K-head. Gates: a scalar decay gate g per (K-head, token) for GDN, or element-wise per-K-dim gate for the KDA template (llama.cpp detects KDA by src_g->ne[0] == S_v); beta (delta-rate) is scalar per V-head, typically sigmoid-normalized. The layer is preceded by a depthwise causal short conv (linear_conv_kernel_dim 4) over the fused q/k/v(z) projection - the 'causal-conv1d' kernel dependency. Tuple view per linear layer: (k,v) = (128,128), state = 48 matrices of 128x128 fp32.
architecture.kv_heads_gqa: No KV cache and no KV heads in the attention sense: linear layers keep no per-token K/V. The analog of the KV head count is the state tensor per layer: 48 value heads x (128x128) fp32 state per sequence on the 27B dense models (= 786,432 elements/layer, ~3.1 MB/layer) plus conv state of width 6144 x (kernel-1 = 3) (~74KB/layer). Per full model per sequence: ~151 MB GDN state + ~3.5 MB conv state in fp32, fixed regardless of context length. The 16 full-attention layers separately carry GQA 6:1 (4 KV heads x 256) KV cache at 64 KiB/token (whole model, fp16).
architecture.hybrid_pattern: 3:1 linear:full expressed as full_attention_interval 4 - 48 GDN + 16 full layers in 64-layer Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8-27B dense; 36 GDN + 12 full in Qwen3-Next-80B; 30 GDN + 10 full in Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. LMSYS (2026-08-26): the GDN+Gated-Attention hybrid is used 'from Qwen3.5 through Qwen3.8'; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next keeps the 3:1 ratio but swaps the full layer for QSA sparse attention. Serving consequence: 75% of layers are O(1)-in-context recurrent layers whose kernels (chunked prefill, recurrent decode, short conv) must be sm_75-portable, while only the 25% full layers need the d=256 attention bridge. MTP adds 1 nextn layer (mtp_num_hidden_layers 1).
architecture.heterogeneous_dims: Yes - the two mechanisms in one model have different dims (linear 128/128 vs full 256/256/256 with 64-dim partial RoPE), so a serving stack must run two disjoint kernel families per forward pass: a GDN backend (vLLM GDN_ATTN / SGLang linear-attn-backend, default triton) and a paged full-attention backend. Within the linear side itself all layers are homogeneous. llama.cpp handles the same split under one graph: gated_delta_net.cu + ssm-conv.cu for linear layers, fattn (with dkq256/dv256 tile instances) for full layers.

kernel_support.supported_dims: Three implementations cover the linear side. (1) FLA Triton (the default everywhere on pre-Hopper): fully generic/autotuned - chunk_gated_delta_rule prefill decomposes into chunk_scaled_dot_kkt, solve_tril, wy_fast, chunk_delta_h (state recurrence), chunk_o (output), cumsum (gate cumsum), l2norm (q/k L2 norm inside the kernel); decode is a per-token fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule kernel (vLLM calls fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode); v-head dims to 256 accepted, chunk size fixed at 64 in vLLM's vendored copy. No per-shape templates and no compute-capability branch other than feature flags (TMA gated to Hopper+; vendored utils query max shared memory per device for autotune). (2) llama.cpp gated_delta_net.cu: template-instantiated S_v {16,32,64,128} + KDA bool + snapshot-slot bool, warp-per-column recurrent kernel, warp-shuffle reductions, fp32 state [S_v,S_v,H,n_seqs], scale 1/sqrt(S_v) - no tensor cores, no dynamic smem, no cp.async, hence arch-agnostic. (3) TFLA/NX-AI mlstm_kernels: Triton with four explicit tile sizes (B_Lhq, B_Lkv, B_dqk, B_dhv), demonstrated head dims 256 and beyond. vLLM additionally ships FlashInfer CUTLASS GDN prefill (SM90; SM100 with k=128 + CUDA runtime >= 13) and CuteDSL prefill (SM100 only) - verified in vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py of the sm75-marlin tree; sm_75 selects the Triton/FLA path for BOTH prefill and decode.
kernel_support.capability_gate: No explicit CC gate blocks the linear side on sm_75 - the gate that matters is inside Triton itself: upstream Triton merged '[BACKEND] Deprecate MMAv1; fallback to FMA for computeCapability < 80' (triton-lang/triton PR #5066, merged 2024-11-05, shipped in Triton 3.3), so tl.dot on Turing lowers to FMA (CUDA-core) loops, not tensor cores; the triton-windows project describes this as 'Turing is supported until Triton 3.2, and Triton 3.3 dropped support' - kernels still compile and run, just without MMA [uncertain - exact behavior of newest Triton releases on sm_75 not executed this session; Triton 3.6.0 demonstrably still compiled a Triton attention kernel on a T4 in vLLM issue #36802, failing only on the 64KB shared-memory limit: 'Required: 81920, Hardware limit: 65536']. Historic Turing-specific Triton bugs: IndexError map::at in tl.dot lowering on 2080Ti (triton#3011, #4813), which FLA issue #179 cites as 'a common bug with NVIDIA Turing architecture' (workaround: disable autotuning); PyTorch Inductor carries an explicit patch around #3011. NVIDIA's toolchain is not the blocker: CUDA 13.x removed only pre-Turing architectures (sm_75 is now the floor).
kernel_support.fallback_semantics: On sm_75 every hybrid-serving stack silently routes the linear layers to Triton/FLA: vLLM's _resolve_gdn_prefill_backend returns 'triton' unless SM90/SM100 (verified in the local tree) and logs 'Falling back to Triton/FLA' only if a non-default backend was explicitly requested; SGLang's --linear-attn-backend defaults to triton. There is no error and no padding - FLA is considered the portable baseline. Failure modes seen in the field are autotune-config related, not arch checks: FLA on T4 hit the Triton map::at bug (issue #179, closed 'no T4 for tests right now' - i.e., no Turing CI) and Triton attention kernels on T4 die with OutOfResources when a config assumes >64KB smem (vLLM #36802). The expected remedy is pinning smaller BK/BV/num_stages configs or disabling autotune rather than a code path change. llama.cpp needs no fallback at all - its GDN kernel is plain CUDA that runs on any sm >= 30-class device with warp shuffles.
kernel_support.ci_hardware_coverage: The linear-attention kernel stack is CI'd only on newer hardware: FLA maintainers explicitly closed the T4 report without testing ('we have no T4 for tests right now', issue #179, 2025); vLLM's GDN vendor kernels are exercised on SM90 (CUTLASS prefill), SM100 (CuteDSL, Gluon), SM120 (tracking issue #18590 items); the PyTorch hybrid-models blog benchmarks H100 only; TFLA benchmarks H100 only. Turing coverage rests entirely on community self-help: triton-windows maintaining a Turing-capable Triton fork, llama.cpp's arch-agnostic CUDA kernel (community Qwen3.8-27B runs on RTX 3080/3090-class cards, discussion #27164), and this project's own sm_75 validation program. Every 'supported' claim for Triton linear-attention kernels is therefore rotting with respect to sm_75: new kernel features (TMA, Gluon, CuteDSL) target Hopper/Blackwell, and the one canonical Turing bug (#3011-class) has been open since 2024 with a PyTorch-side patch rather than an upstream fix.

performance.turing_baseline: No published sm_75 measurements of FLA/Triton Gated DeltaNet kernels exist as of 2026-09 [uncertain - absence-of-evidence after targeted search of GitHub issues, FLA repo, vLLM/SGLang docs, and community posts]. Adjacent data points: (a) Triton-on-Turing loses tensor cores for tl.dot since Triton 3.3 (PR #5066 deprecates MMAv1 below sm_80), so chunked prefill pays FMA-only dot products; the recurrent decode kernel is bandwidth/launch-bound rather than mma-bound, so its sm_75 deficit should be smaller [uncertain - reasoned, not measured]. (b) Nearest hardware class with numbers: RTX 3090 (Ampere sm_86, 24GB) runs Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 at 82 tok/s single request, up to 672 tok/s peak under concurrency (Reddit r/LocalLLaMA, 2026), and dual-3090 vLLM walkthroughs exist for Qwen3.6-27B; on a single GA100 sm_80 a Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 MTP-off decode was profiled in vLLM #35387 comments. (c) Negative datapoint: Triton attention (not GDN) fails to launch on T4 due to smem (vLLM #36802). (d) llama.cpp serves Qwen3.8-27B GGUF on 16GB-class Turing/Ampere consumer cards (autodidacts.io RTX 3080 report, per sibling item). Local project anchor: none yet - the flashinfer-sm75-validation work covers only full attention at d=128/256; an FLA-GDN microbench on sm_75 is the missing baseline.
performance.d256_feasibility: For the LINEAR side this question is moot in practice: Qwen's GDN heads are 128/128 and every implementation covers them portably - FLA autotunes generically (v-head up to 256), llama.cpp instantiates S_v=128, and the 128x128 fp32 state shard per V-head fits trivially in Turing's 64KB smem if chunked kernels even use smem (the llama.cpp recurrent kernel uses registers only: rows_per_lane = S_v/warp_size = 4 fp32 registers for state + k/q). If a future model used v_dim 256 linear heads, FLA still accepts it (generic autotune), but on sm_75 the chunked prefill would need configs that fit 64KB smem (BV 64 chunks of a 256-wide V are 64KB in bf16 alone) - feasible but requiring manual config pinning like the T4 autotune workarounds. The binding d=256 constraint of these models remains the 25% full-attention layers, served separately by the bridge routes; the constant-size state means the linear side adds ~154 MB/sequence regardless of head-dim scaling.
performance.cost_analysis: Quantified costs of serving the linear side: (1) State memory: GDN state 48 layers x 48 V-heads x 128x128 fp32 = 151 MB/sequence (77 MB/GPU at TP2) + conv state ~3.5 MB/seq, context-independent - versus 64 KiB/token of full-attention KV (16 layers x 2048 elements x 2B fp16): the crossover where one sequence's KV exceeds all its linear state is ~2,400 tokens; at 128k context KV is ~8 GB vs 0.15 GB linear state (the PyTorch blog's ~200x figure for Nemotron at 128k). State is the batch-scaling memory term (max_num_seqs x 154 MB), KV the context term. (2) Compute structure: chunked prefill with chunk 64 (FLA) parallelizes over chunks but performs a serial intra-batch state recurrence (chunk_delta_h); TFLA's paper shows H100-runtime optimum at chunk 128-256 and that 'newer hardware generations require larger chunk sizes' - implying sm_75 wants chunk <= 64-128, consistent with FLA's 64; TFLA's nested tiling removes the SRAM ceiling on chunk size (the mechanism a 64KB-smem Turing port would need) and bought ~25% over naive chunked kernels on H100. (3) Launch overhead: Triton CPU launch overhead (triton#2637) is severe for 75 recurrent+conv layers per token - the driver behind FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs (up to +91% throughput vs PIECEWISE at low concurrency on granite-4.0-h-tiny, H100, PyTorch blog). (4) MTP cost: verification of 2 tokens costs 1.79x one token on Qwen3.5-4B (GDN layers make verify non-free, #35387 comment); graph downgrade cost scales linearly with draft depth; MTP n=2 cost +76.5% latency on the #35387 repro. (5) llama.cpp has no chunked prefill ('TODO: Add chunked kernel for even faster pre-fill'), so its prefill is token-serial: O(T) kernel iterations per layer.

design_fit.route: Informs the bridge plan from the OUTSIDE: the 75% linear layers never touch the d=256 attention bridge at all - on sm_75 they are served by head-shape-generic Triton/FLA (vLLM GDN_ATTN, SGLang linear-attn-backend=triton) exactly like route C's philosophy (generic, JIT/autotuned coverage over fixed templates), and llama.cpp proves a plain-CUDA recurrent kernel covers sm_75 with zero portability work. The bridge routes A/B/C apply only to the remaining 25% full-attention layers. The item's own 'route' lesson: budget engineering for the linear side as a RUNTIME-contract problem (CUDA-graph modes, state pool sizing, MTP state rollback), not a kernel-shape problem.
design_fit.recommendation: For the sm_75 Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 plan: (1) keep GDN layers on the stock FLA Triton path (prefill chunk 64 + fused_recurrent decode) - it is the only maintained path on pre-Hopper and needs only config hygiene: pre-pin/limit autotune configs to <= 64KB smem and verify against the Triton map::at Turing bug family (#3011); test Triton 3.2-vs-3.3+ (MMAv1 deprecation) to decide whether to pin an older Triton for tensor-core tl.dot on sm_75. (2) Satisfy the runtime contract rather than rewriting kernels: UNIFORM_BATCH cudagraph support with decode-only full graphs (+FULL_AND_PIECEWISE), unified mamba/KV page alignment (vLLM already does this), causal-conv1d via vLLM's in-tree Triton implementation (no pip dep needed). (3) Do NOT enable TurboQuant KV + MTP + chunked prefill together (#40807 crash, PR #43747 pending) and benchmark MTP before shipping it (#35387: +76% latency; GDN verify costs ~1.8x/token) - on a Turing box the graph-downgrade penalty will be worse than on H100. (4) Treat llama.cpp's gated_delta_net.cu as the sm_75 reference if FLA misbehaves: a ~200-line warp-shuffle CUDA kernel, template S_v=128, Turing-safe, with state-snapshot slots for speculative rollback. Next action: run the FLA chunk_gated_delta_rule + fused_recurrent kernels through the local sm_75 harness at (HK=128, HV=128, HV=48) Qwen3.8-27B shapes and record a turing_baseline.
design_fit.numerics_risks: GDN accumulation order is observable and load-bearing: SGLang preserves 'the reference FP32 accumulation order and bitwise-identical outputs' in its fused GDN paths and its Triton GDN output-state mismatch with FLA is a live bug class (sglang #18610); llama.cpp keeps everything fp32 (state, q/k/v/g/beta read as fp32, warp-shuffle reduction order fixed by lane layout). A Triton-FMA fallback on sm_75 changes tl.dot lowering and hence accumulation grouping vs sm80 MMA - outputs remain fp32-accurate (FMA is not less precise, just reordered) but bitwise expectations must be relaxed. The delta-rule state update S = g*S + k*delta with g=exp(gate) can decay/overflow under fp16 - keep state and gate cumsum in fp32 (FLA does; the cumsum of log-decays is its own kernel). The short-conv state and the q/k L2-norm inside FLA kernels must not be re-fused away. Turing's lack of BF16 forces an fp16 activation + fp32 state mix that upstream kernels see rarely. Known wrong-output history: Triton Turing tl.dot map::at (#3011/#4813, silent until crash), FLA-Triton vs FLA reference state mismatches (sglang #18610), and the fused llama.cpp GDN kernel that regressed perf 39% (b8333, Metal) shows fusion bugs are an active risk. MTP adds rollback correctness: rejected tokens must restore GDN state (vLLM spec_state_indices + num_accepted_tokens path; llama.cpp keep_rs snapshot slots) - #35387/#39809/#43559 show this path is where correctness bugs cluster.
design_fit.demand_weighting: Very high for the Turing installed base: 75% of the layers of the default local-model family (Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8) are linear, and their kernels are the ONLY part of the stack that already runs portably on sm_75 - so a Turing user's ability to serve these models hinges on (a) this linear side working, and (b) the 25% full-attention bridge. Cloud T4 fleets (still the cheapest ubiquitous inference GPU) get the linear side for free with Triton but are blocked by the d=256 full layers; 24GB-class owners (Titan RTX/Quadro RTX 6000 2x24GB) can weight-quantize into range precisely because the linear layers keep state constant (154 MB/seq) instead of KV. llama.cpp demand validates this: Qwen3.5/3.8 GGUF on 16-24GB consumer cards is a top community topic, and #15940's GDN implementation was the sole hard part. Vendors are moving the other way (CuteDSL/Gluon/FlashInfer GDN kernels are SM90/SM100-only), so sm_75 coverage will not arrive from upstream - it is a community/bridge-project play, with linear-attention coverage already solved and full-attention d=256 the residual gap.
